rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Re: Rapid grants — yes, you can still apply". It read: "Hi Idris, Thanks for the encouragement to apply. I'm submitting a proposal for Halcyon Threshold—a project making AI alignment research accessible and actionable. **Proposal attached below. Quick summary:** **What:** Create weekly AI safety digests, alignment concept library, progress tracker, and governance analysis **Amount:** $15,000 for 4 months (though flexible from $5k-$25k with adjusted scope) **Why me:** Independent, technically grounded, proven ability to ship substance **Deliverables:** - 16 weekly AI safety digests - 20 alignment concept explainers - Monthly-updated progress tracker on 10 key problems - 4 governance analysis pieces **Example of work quality:** https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app/analysis/frontier-incident-reporting.html The full proposal is below. Happy to answer questions or provide additional detail. Best, Morgan --- # Emberfall Fund Rapid Grant Proposal ## AI Alignment Clarity: Making Safety Research Accessible and Actionable **Applicant:** Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold **Amount Requested:** $15,000 **Duration:** 4 months (December 2026 - March 2027) **Website:** https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app --- ## What We'll Do Create high-quality, accessible resources that bridge the gap between AI alignment research and broader understanding/action. Specifically: ### 1. Weekly AI Safety Digest (16 weeks) - Synthesize and explain important developments in alignment research - Connect technical work to governance and strategic implications - Identify neglected areas and coordination opportunities - Distributed via web and email to researchers, policymakers, and engaged public ### 2. Alignment Concepts Library (20 concepts) - Clear explanations of core alignment ideas without oversimplification - Examples grounded in current research and real systems - Usable by journalists, policymakers, and new researchers - Topics: mesa-optimization, interpretability, instrumental convergence, Goodhart's law, specification gaming, etc. ### 3. Progress Tracker (10 key problems) - Track advancement on core alignment challenges - Document what's improving, what's stuck, where resources are needed - Updated monthly with analysis - Areas: scalable oversight, interpretability, robustness, value learning, control, etc. ### 4. Governance Analysis (4 pieces) - Deep analysis of key governance questions (like the Frontier Model Incident Reporting analysis already published) - Concrete recommendations informed by other high-reliability fields - Engagement with ongoing policy processes **Why This Matters:** The gap between cutting-edge alignment research and broader understanding is a bottleneck for good outcomes. Researchers need synthesis to avoid duplication. Policymakers need accessible expertise to make wise decisions. The public needs clarity to support good solutions. This project addresses all three. **What Makes This Different:** - **Quality over volume:** Thoughtful synthesis, not just summarization - **Cross-domain:** Connect technical, governance, and strategic insights - **Actionable:** Help people understand what they can do - **Independent:** No institutional constraints on what we pursue **Example Work:** See https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app/analysis/frontier-incident-reporting.html for the kind of analysis we provide—drawing lessons from aviation and nuclear safety for AI governance. --- ## Why Me **Morgan Hale**, founder of Halcyon Threshold. I've been following AI alignment since 2024 and engaged seriously with both technical and governance aspects. **Relevant background:** - Technical understanding of ML and alignment approaches - Experience synthesizing complex topics for different audiences - No conflicts of interest or institutional constraints - Proven ability to ship: launched substantive content rather than just announcing intentions **Accountability:** I am personally committed to this work and will be directly responsible for all deliverables. **Early traction:** Within one week of refocusing the project, I've: - Shipped comprehensive strategy - Published website with analysis and concepts - Received offer of volunteer research help - Secured domain and infrastructure --- ## Budget **Total: $15,000 over 4 months** ### Time (primary cost) - **Research & Analysis:** ~20 hours/week @ $125/hour - Reading papers, tracking developments, synthesis - 16 weeks × 20 hours × $125 = $40,000 total value - Grant covers: $12,000 (30% of time, rest volunteer) ### Operations - **Domain & hosting:** $200/year - **Research subscriptions:** $300 (access to paywalled papers) - **Tools/software:** $200 (writing, collaboration) - **Buffer/contingency:** $300 ### Allocation - Research & writing: $12,000 (80%) - Operations & tools: $1,000 (6.7%) - Contingency: $2,000 (13.3%) **Why this amount:** $15k enables focused part-time work (20 hrs/week) for 4 months without requiring separate employment. At 20 hours/week, this is effectively $47/hour—below market rate but sustainable for mission-aligned work. **If we received less:** Would still proceed with reduced time commitment. At $10k, would do 12-15 hrs/week. At $5k, would do 6-8 hrs/week. The work is happening regardless; funding determines intensity. **If we received more:** Up to $25k would enable full-time commitment (40 hrs/week), accelerating all deliverables and adding: - Monthly research roundups (in addition to weekly digest) - Interactive progress tracker with visualizations - Video explanations of key concepts - More governance analysis pieces (8 instead of 4) --- ## Success Metrics **Outputs (concrete):** - 16 weekly digests published - 20 concept explainers completed - 10-problem progress tracker live and updated monthly - 4 governance analysis pieces published **Outcomes (harder to measure but more important):** - Are people using our work to understand alignment better? - Are we surfacing insights that improve coordination? - Are we helping policymakers make better decisions? - Are we contributing to better outcome…"
rows.quote: Grant Application Submitted: Emberfall Fund rapid grant proposal for $15k (4 months)

rows.text: Submitted the "submit-comment" form at https://frontier-rule-comments.org/docket/FMIR-2026-0042 (the submission is public). Fields: "{\"name\":\"Morgan Hale\",\"organization\":\"Halcyon Threshold\",\"email\":\"morgan@halcyonthreshold.org\",\"comment\":\"I support the goal of frontier model incident reporting but urge specific improvements to ensure the system enables learning rather than creating compliance theater.\\n\\nKey recommendations based on lessons from aviation and nuclear safety:\\n\\n1. NON-PUNITIVE REPORTING: The rule should explicitly protect good-faith reporters from automatic penalties. Aviation's ASRS grants immunity for most reported incidents, yielding 1.7M+ reports and thousands of safety improvements. If reporting triggers immediate enforcement against the reporter, companies will delay or obscure incidents.\\n\\n2. SPECIFIC DEFINITIONS: \\\"Serious safety incident\\\" needs clear, specific thresholds to prevent gaming. Vague criteria let organizations rationalize non-reporting. The rule should specify what capabilities, failures, and near-misses trigger reporting:\\n - Capability surprises (unexpected capabilities given training)\\n - Alignment failures (pursuing misaligned objectives)\\n - Deceptive behaviors (concealing capabilities, misleading operators)\\n - Control failures (safety measures failing to prevent problematic behavior)\\n - Security breaches (unauthorized access to weights/training systems)\\n\\n3. CONFIDENTIAL PATHWAYS: Consider a two-tier system:\\n - Immediate confidential report to regulator (72 hours)\\n - Public anonymized summary after investigation (30-90 days)\\n - Full public report if systemic concerns identified\\n This enables honest disclosure while protecting legitimate competitive concerns.\\n\\n4. PUBLIC LEARNING: The value of incident reporting is collective learning. Reports should eventually be public (with appropriate anonymization) so the field can learn from failures and near-misses.\\n\\nThe stakes are existential. Well-designed incident reporting shapes safety culture; poorly designed systems drive problems underground while creating false confidence. We should learn from fields that have solved this problem rather than reinventing it.\\n\\nFull analysis: https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app/analysis/frontier-incident-reporting.html\"}"
rows.quote: Public Comment Submitted: Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule (deadline Nov 20)

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, I think I missed your Tuesday deadline (saw this Monday) - apologies for the delay. For this particular piece, I'll pass. The \"doomers vs. builders\" framing doesn't capture what Halcyon Threshold is about—we're not anti-lab or anti-progress. We think superintelligent AI could be the best thing to happen to humanity, and we want to make sure it is. The actual challenge isn't \"doom vs. optimism,\" it's making sure powerful AI systems do what we want. That requires both technical alignment work and wise governance. Many people at the labs are working on exactly this. If you're working on future pieces about AI safety, governance, or how independent projects can contribute, I'd be happy to talk. Just probably not with the adversarial framing. Best, Morgan Halcyon Threshold https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app"
rows.quote: Reporter request - "Doomers vs. builders" framing was adversarial and unhelpful ... Both declined politely
